chapter_title: Concerning the Three Images that are in the righte

spiritual_reading.full_translation:
In a person being renewed there appear three distinct forms in which life is received and shown.

First, there is an inmost form: higher illumination forms within the person a new will and a new understanding, and this new human is introduced into the person and abides as an interior presence.

Second, there is an intermediate form: what remains of that new human as it is held within the natural self. At this middle level the renewed things are still bound within hereditary selfhood and its acquired habits, because this degree still carries what was formed when the natural self ruled.

Third, there is an outermost form added beneath them, in which life is expressed in the lowest degree through outward action and sensory appearance.

These three forms act together as one process. As the person is sustained by what is received from without, the person’s life is alternately raised toward what is inmost and lowered toward what is outermost, according to the way reception is made. When the life is lowered into the lowest form, the outermost level strips off what does not belong to the person’s proper spiritual life and transfers what can be set in order into the intermediate level. Then the life rises and falls again toward the middle, and in this movement it casts off the middle-level impurities that cling from hostile influences—especially the excitations that inflame contentious anger. Disordered craving also clings and is carried along until it too is separated.

After this, a pure guiding perception from higher illumination approaches and discloses the inmost form that is present, the new human. That guiding illumination goes before, elevating what can be elevated into higher states, and what is elevated is received into the inmost form. It gives the new human determinate shape and orders it with what is renewed within, until the renewal is confirmed and fully organized by all the powers of that illumination which is present and makes its dwelling within the new human.

In this way the living power in a person is purified and truly lives, even as it enters the life of one being made righteous from without through the continual reception of mental sustenance in varied ways. The living soul is to be wholly cleansed each day, and to pass through these three forms of life in their order.

Thus it casts off the outermost selfhood that is not truly its own in the lowest degree. It also casts off the foreign life-admixtures that are not its own, which are mingled in the intermediate degree: irritations, cravings, dullness of mind, empty thinking, jealousy, contention, and similar evils, together with false teachings that do not originate from the new life.

But in the inmost form itself it lives, and it is conjoined with patient endurance, with the completeness of faith, and with love that governs all things in right order. This governing illumination is what invests the new human with living truth, and it is called the turning-point at which life begins. It is first in the work of renewal, and it is also last, because it is the beginning within every stage and the final confirmation of the whole.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Coheres strongly as a three-degree doctrine of regeneration with alternation of elevation and descent and progressive casting off of what is not one’s own. The main stumble is paragraph 6’s broken syntax, but its intended cycle—external sustenance, alternation of state, and successive purgation—still carries through as one voice into the disclosure and confirmation of the inmost new human.

findings.diagnosis: Clean chapter incipit: a simple threefold schema announcement that sets up a functional (process) teaching and is then used consistently.
findings.evidence: Text: “Three images occur in the elect person.” The spiritual reading treats this as “three distinct forms… in which life is received and shown,” and the rest of the chapter actually develops these three as stages/modes of one purification process (¶6–10). No foreign names, jurisdictions, or inventory logic appears.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential definition of the first (highest) image as an interior formation; the spiritual sense arises from what it does (forms/dwells), not from who rules it.
findings.evidence: Text: “the spiritual image… the new man… the Light Mind shall form in him; and it goes into him and dwells in him.” The reading’s move (“higher illumination forms… introduced… abides”) follows the functional verbs “form,” “goes into,” “dwells.” No administrative rank/jurisdiction markers.

findings.diagnosis: Genuine difficulty from textual damage/awkward transmission inside an otherwise coherent correspondential paragraph; the reading stumbles because the Coptic/translation line is broken, not because a different voice intruded.
findings.evidence: Text is internally fractured: “as the old man [is being preserved in the flesh] times of this psychic image.” The spiritual reading explicitly notes: “source sentence is partly broken (‘old man… times’).” Despite the break, the paragraph still continues the same functional teaching (a ‘remnant… bound in the flesh’), so excision would not improve narrative flow; it would only remove the middle term the chapter needs.

findings.diagnosis: Clean completion of the threefold structure with a third ‘corporeal’ image; it is necessary for the later cycling/‘divesting’ mechanics in ¶6 and remains in the same functional voice.
findings.evidence: Text: “The other one is the corporeal image [that is] added to them all.” The later process explicitly depends on ‘sink… down to the corporeal image’ and transfers upward (¶6). The reading’s “outermost form added beneath them” matches the functional role ‘added’ / ‘beneath’.

findings.diagnosis: Genuine difficulty due to heavy corruption/ellipsis in a key process paragraph (state-changes + divesting/transfer). The spiritual reading’s only real ‘stumble’ is syntactic, not conceptual; the underlying voice remains correspondential and continuous with ¶7–10.
findings.evidence: Text shows multiple bracketed lacunae and tangled pronominal reference: “These three images [operate] entirely. When it will [be elevated]… If it shall sink… [And] the corporeal, [that] is in it, shall divest itself of it and place it…” The reading notes: “paragraph’s syntax is fragmented,” and therefore paraphrases (“alternately raised… lowered… strips off… transfers”). Nothing here shifts into governance/jurisdiction; instead it is functional mechanics: elevation/sinking, divesting, transferring, and passions (‘anger’, ‘lust’) as operative states.

findings.diagnosis: Clean continuation: the ‘light virgin’ functions as an operative mechanism (guide/reveal/seal/organize) within the purification process, not as an administrative office-holder. Personified imagery is still correspondential because it explains what the agent does in the transformation.
findings.evidence: Text: “a light virgin come and reveal… acts as a guide… goes on before… received… she [sculpts] it and adorns it… It is sealed with all the limbs of this light virgin…” The reading explicitly renders these as functional operations (“guiding perception… discloses… elevating… gives shape… confirmed/organized by all the powers”). There is no list of subordinate rulers, stations, or territorial control; the figure participates actively in the process, so it is not a dropped-in name list.

findings.diagnosis: Clean but with one minor potential seam-word (‘administration’) that could mislead; here it still means practical mediation via food, integrated into the functional narrative of daily purification. Not an administrative-voice overlay.
findings.evidence: Text: “through the administration of food of various kinds.” The term “administration” can resemble governance vocabulary, but the sentence immediately grounds it in function and process: nourishment entering “from without,” daily cleansing, and traversing “these three images.” The spiritual reading notes it as “outward nourishment… varied external means,” and the narrative continues seamlessly into the divesting list (¶9). No jurisdictions or authorities are assigned.

findings.diagnosis: Clean ethical unpacking of what gets ‘divested’ at each level; it directly implements the mechanics of ¶6 and stays in correspondential/functional language (not owned vs not its own; mixed states).
findings.evidence: Text: “divest itself of the body, which is not its own… divest itself of the souls that are not its own… mixed with it… anger and desire and [dull]-ness…” The reading tracks this exactly as level-specific purification (“outermost… intermediate… foreign admixtures”). This is not an inventory of officials; it’s a diagnostic list of states to be purged.

findings.diagnosis: Clean culmination: positive end-state (faith/love/longsuffering) and identification of the ‘virgin of light’ as the robing/confirming agent; ‘first and last’ is an internal rhetorical closure, not a later administrative taxonomy.
findings.evidence: Text: “joined with long-sufferingness… perfection of faith and love that reigns over them all. It is the virgin of light who robes the new man… called ‘the hour of life’. She is the first… also the last.” The reading flags no narrative break; it treats this as the governing inner principle that begins and completes the process. No switch to jurisdictional language beyond metaphorical “reigns,” which here functions as ‘governs in order’ rather than institutional authority.

textual_criticism.summary: No administrative overlay blocks and no clear insertions/expansions are indicated by the spiritual reading. The chapter is overwhelmingly correspondential/functional and narratively coherent as a three-image purification cycle. The only real stumbles are genuine textual damage/ellipsis in ¶4 and especially ¶6 (broken syntax and pronominal confusion), plus a minor mixed-vocabulary risk at ¶8 (“administration”) that remains contextually functional. Recommended actions: 0 excisions, 0 annotations, 10 ‘none’ (with ¶4 and ¶6 noted as damaged transmission rather than voice intrusion).

harmonized_paragraphs.text: Three images occur in the elect person.
The first is the spiritual image, which is the new man, which the Light Mind shall form in him; and it goes into him and dwells in him.
The second image is the remnant and remainder of the new man, which is the psychic image that is bound in the flesh, as the old man [is being preserved in the flesh] times of this psychic image.
The other one is the corporeal image [that is] added to them all.

These three images [operate] entirely. When it will [be elevated] through the nourishment of food. If it shall sink [into it] down to the corporeal image. [And] the corporeal, [that] is in it, shall divest itself of it and place it in the [psychic] image. [Then] again it rises up and falls to the [psychic] image; it shall divest itself of the psychical of the enemies, which [inflame and stir up] anger. The lust [also clings and is carried along] with it.

Then shall a light virgin come and reveal the spiritual image that is [there], which [is] the new man. That virgin acts as a guide. [She g]oes on before and it is extended to the heights above, and received into this spiritual image. And she [sculpts] it and adorns it with the new man [wi]thin. It is sealed with all the limbs of this light virgin who is present and dwells in the new man.

So, this is [h]ow this living limb shall be [puri]fied and live, the one that comes into the body of [the ri]ghteous one from without through the administration of food of various ki[nds], like this. The living soul shall be clea[n]sed entirely every [d]ay and traverse these three [im]a[ges].

So, it shall divest itself of the body, which is not its own, in the corporeal. It shall also divest itself of the souls that are not its own, these that are mixed with it in the psychical [especially in] anger and desire and [dull]-ness and foolishness and envy and strife; and these other wicked teachings that are not its own.

However, in [the] spiritual image itself it shall live and be joined with [lo]ng-sufferingness, the perfection of faith and love that reigns over them all. It is the virgin of light who robes the new man and who shall be cal[l]ed ‘the hour of life’. S[he] is the f[irst], but s[h]e is also the last.

changes_summary: No changes made. The critic’s findings recommend ‘none’ for all paragraphs (Findings 1–9), with ¶4 and ¶6 noted as damaged transmission rather than insertions, and no excisions indicated.
